Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 79 s. 2023 DEC 18 Datu Dadantulan Enabangan Clan Leader Office of the Tribal Council of Nababalay Ya Ininay Ta Sinakungan Natumbawan Esperanza, Agusan Del Sur Dear Datu Dadantulan: This has reference to the Resolution received by this Department on June 22, 2023 pertaining to the request for a copy of notification of termination of jurisdiction over the ancestral domain previously held by other government agencies, including this Office. The request is in connection with Sec. 52 (i)l of The Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997 (IPRA) which terminated any legal basis of the aforementioned government agencies' claim over the ancestral domains. Attached in the request is a copy of the Certificate of Recognition of Ancestral Domain with CADT No. R13-ESP-1021-255 marked as Annex "A" The Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 8371 or the Indigenous Peoples Rights Act (IPRA) has defined the Certificate of Ancestral Domain (CADT) as a title formally recognizing the right of possession and ownership of ICCs/lPs over their ancestral domains identified and delineated in accordance with law. Hence, public lands will be considered as private lands, and never to have been part of a public domain area once declared and recognized with the CADT. The subject provision found under Sec. II substantially provides the salient features of a CADT, to wit: SECTION II. Recognition of Ancestral Domain Rights. - The rights of ICCs/lPs to their ancestral domains by virtue of Native Title shall be recognized and respected. Formal recognition, when solicited by ICCs/IPs concerned, shall be embodied in a Certificate of Ancestral Domain Title (CADT), which shall recognize the title of the concerned ICCs/IPs over the territories identified and delineated. 1 i) Turnover of Areas Within Ancestral Domains Managed by Other Government Agencies. — The Chairperson of the NCIP shall certify that the area covered is an ancestral domain. The secretaries of the Department of Agrarian Reform, Department of Environment and Natural Resources. Department of the Interior and Local Government, and Department of Justice. the Commissioner of the National Development Corporation, and any other government agency claiming jurisdiction over the area shall be notified thereof. Such notification shall terminate any legal basis for the jurisdiction previously claimed; "Matlno, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Moreover, the High Court has declared that the concept of ownership and title for indigenous people are not dependent on a piece of paper, instead, a paper title is merely seen as a formal recognition of native title. In Lamsis, et al. v. Dong-e2,we held - The application for issuance of a Certificate of Ancestral Land Title pending before the NCIP is akin to a registration proceeding. It also seeks an official recognition of one's claim to a particular land and is also in rem. The titling of ancestral lands is for the purpose of "officially establishing" one's land as an ancestral land. Just like a registration proceeding, the titling of ancestral lands does not vest ownership upon the applicant but only recognizes ownership that has already vested in the applicant by virtue of his and his predecessor-in-interest's possession of the property since time immemorial. As aptly explained in another case: It bears stressing at this point that ownership should not be confused with a certificate of title. Registering land under the Torrens system does not create or vest title because registration is not a mode of acquiring ownership. A certificate of title is merely an evidence of ownership or title over the particular property described therein. A closer scrutiny of par (3) under CADT No. R13-ESP-1021-2553 expressly provides the notice of termination of the exercise of jurisdiction exercised by the government agencies concerned, we quote in verbatim: WHEREAS, the Recognition of the Higaonon-Banwaon Indigenous Peoples and their Ancestral Domain (AD) is hereby certified to and pursuant to Section 52 (i) of IPRA, this Certification effectively TERMINATES any legal basis for the jurisdiction that may be previously claimed over the ancestral domain on the part of the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), the Department of Justice (DOJ), the National Development Corporation (NDC), and any other government agency claiming jurisdiction over the said ancestral domain. [emphasis supplied] Hence, we opine that the issuance of this subject document from the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) is conclusive proof, which effectively and sufficiently terminates any legal basis for the jurisdiction that may be previously claimed on the part of the government agencies concerned. Considering the foregoing, we find that no other document is needed for the turnover of areas within Ancestral Domains managed by other government agencies, except the CADT. 2 G.R. No. 173021, October 20, 2010. Annex "A". Page 2 of 3

Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you.
